entity.name: mini_cpu_core_top
entity.description: Design a small CPU core project in VHDL, choosing either a mini RISC-V subset or a coherent custom 8-bit ISA, with a complete fetch/decode/execute path and deterministic verification.

behavior: Design a small CPU core project in VHDL, choosing either a mini RISC-V subset or a coherent custom 8-bit ISA, with a complete fetch/decode/execute path and deterministic verification.
Required block/responsibility: instruction fetch path with program counter management
Required block/responsibility: ALU with clearly defined supported operations
Required block/responsibility: control unit or control FSM
Required block/responsibility: branch/jump or control-flow handling
Required block/responsibility: top-level CPU integration entity
State the chosen ISA subset or custom instruction set clearly.
Define operand widths, register count, and memory interface semantics explicitly.
Keep decode, execute, and state-update behavior understandable rather than opaque.
Assume a single clock domain for the core and document any alternative choice explicitly.
Reset must place the CPU into a deterministic fetch-ready state.
Avoid gated clocks and uncontrolled combinational feedback between control and datapath blocks.
corner_cases: The testbench must prove fetch, decode, execute, register update, and control-flow behavior with deterministic checks.
Include representative arithmetic, logical, load/store, and branch-style scenarios where supported by the chosen ISA.
prohibited_implementations: Do not describe the CPU as complete while omitting decode or write-back behavior.
Do not use placeholder pseudo-instructions without implementing them in the RTL and testbench.
Do not hide the memory interface behind undocumented magic constants or comments.
synthesis_requirements: Generated RTL and testbench must compile, elaborate, and simulate under GHDL.
The testbench must verify successful execution of a short deterministic instruction sequence.
The generated collateral must make the architectural split between datapath and control clear.
testbench_obligations: The testbench must prove fetch, decode, execute, register update, and control-flow behavior with deterministic checks.
Include representative arithmetic, logical, load/store, and branch-style scenarios where supported by the chosen ISA.
